title: Sub-extensive non-stabilizerness in the Dyck-Fredkin spin chain
abstract: The stabilizer Rényi entropy is a quantitative measure of non-stabilizerness, or magic, and has typically been found to scale extensively with system size $N$ (i.e., $Θ(N)$) for a variety of many-body quantum states. In this note, we study the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the ground state of the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Dyck-Fredkin chain and its $t$-deformation, a local frustration-free model with unusual spectral-gap scaling. Exploiting the combinatorial structure, we carry out numerically exact finite-size calculations, which indicate asymptotic behavior depending on $t$: $Θ(N)$ for $t<1$, $Θ(\log N)$ at $t=1$, and $Θ(1)$ for $t>1$. The scaling at $t=1$ could be another manifestation of the unconventional criticality of the model, while the contrast with the behavior of the entanglement entropy suggests that non-stabilizerness might provide a new window into quantum many-body systems.
summary: This work analyzes the scaling of the stabilizer Rényi entropy in the Dyck-Fredkin spin chain under a deformation parameter $t$. The key finding is that the SRE displays distinct scaling laws ($\Theta(N)$, $\Theta(\log N)$, or $\Theta(1)$) depending on $t$. This suggests that non-stabilizerness is a powerful diagnostic tool capable of revealing unique signatures of quantum criticality beyond what entanglement entropy can measure.
main_problem: The study investigates the scaling behavior of the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) as a quantitative measure of non-stabilizerness in quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The SRE exhibits distinct scaling behaviors ($\Theta(N)$, $\Theta(\log N)$, or $\Theta(1)$) depending on the deformation parameter $t$ of the Dyck-Fredkin chain, suggesting non-stabilizerness provides a unique probe for criticality.
method: The authors use numerical exact finite-size calculations, employing the replica formulation of the SRE, to analyze the asymptotic scaling of the ground state entropy.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the spin-1/2 Dyck-Fredkin chain and its $t$-deformation, a local frustration-free model with unusual spectral-gap scaling.
key_observables: Stabilizer Rényi entropy ($\alpha$-SRE), entanglement entropy, and the spectral gap ($\Delta E$).
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $t$, which defines three distinct regimes: $t < 1$, $t = 1$, and $t > 1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the SRE provides a physically meaningful measure of non-stabilizerness that can distinguish critical points from entanglement entropy.
figures_summary: Figure 3 illustrates the 2-SRE scaling for the deformed chain, showing linear ($t<1$), logarithmic ($t=1$), and constant ($t>1$) behavior, contrasting with entanglement entropy scaling.
paper_structure: The paper introduces SRE as a measure of non-stabilizerness, details the numerical methods for calculating the entropy, and then presents the core results by analyzing the scaling of SRE across the three regimes defined by the parameter $t$.
why_interesting: The finding that SRE exhibits anomalous logarithmic scaling at $t=1$, while entanglement entropy does not, suggests that non-stabilizerness can reveal unique aspects of unconventional quantum criticality not captured by standard entanglement measures.
